Keywords: simple, simplicity, keep it simple, complexity, over-engineering
Description: Prefer the simplest solution that meets the requirement.
Apply When: Choosing between designs; reviewing clever code.
Violation Signs: Abstractions with one implementation; configuration nobody changes; code that needs a comment to be understood.

Keywords: you aren't gonna need it, future proof, speculative, over-engineering, scope
Description: Do not build for needs you do not have yet.
Violation Signs: Hooks and options for hypothetical callers; generic frameworks for one use case.

Keywords: dry, duplication, copy paste, abstraction, rule of three
Description: Remove duplicated knowledge, but wait for the third occurrence before abstracting.
Violation Signs: The same rule changed in several places per change; or the opposite, premature abstractions coupling unrelated code.

Keywords: single responsibility, srp, cohesion, god class, one reason to change
Description: A module should have one reason to change.
Violation Signs: Files touched by unrelated changes; classes named Manager or Utils doing everything.

Keywords: separation of concerns, layers, coupling, business logic, presentation, io
Description: Keep business logic apart from I/O, presentation and framework code.
Apply When: Designing features and refactoring tangled code.
Violation Signs: SQL in UI handlers; business rules that cannot be tested without a database or HTTP server.

Keywords: dependency inversion, dependencies, architecture, layering, imports, boundaries
Description: Dependencies point toward stable, high-level policy; details depend on abstractions, not the reverse.
Violation Signs: Domain code importing framework, database or vendor SDK types; import cycles.

Keywords: types, type safety, invalid state, validation, parse don't validate
Description: Design data types so invalid combinations cannot be constructed.
Apply When: Modeling domain data and API inputs.
Violation Signs: Many boolean flags; optional fields that are required in practice; validation scattered everywhere.

Keywords: fail fast, assert, validate input, error early, crash early, guard clause
Description: Detect invalid state at the boundary and fail loudly instead of continuing with bad data.
Apply When: Input handling, configuration and error handling.
Violation Signs: Errors swallowed and logged; nulls passed deep into the system; defaults that hide misconfiguration.

Keywords: least surprise, naming, consistency, conventions, expectations
Description: Code should behave the way its name and its neighbors suggest.
Violation Signs: Getters with side effects; functions that do more than their name says; inconsistent conventions.

Keywords: measure, profile first, data driven, optimization, benchmark
Description: Optimize only what measurement shows matters, and measure again after.
Violation Signs: Optimizations without numbers; complexity added for speed nobody measured.

Keywords: reversible, rollback, undo, two way door, safe deploy, backward compatible
Description: Favor changes that can be undone quickly; make irreversible steps last and deliberate.
Violation Signs: Destructive migrations without backups; deploys with no rollback path.

Keywords: deterministic, clock, time, random seed, nondeterminism, flaky
Description: Pass time, randomness and external I/O in as dependencies so behavior is reproducible.
Apply When: Code with time, randomness or concurrency, and its tests.
Violation Signs: Direct calls to now() and random() inside logic; tests that sleep.
